voyager1.name: Voyager 1
voyager1.blurb: Most distant human-made object; crossed into interstellar space in 2012, still returning data from beyond the heliopause.

voyager2.name: Voyager 2
voyager2.blurb: Only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune; now in interstellar space on a different trajectory than Voyager 1.

pioneer10.name: Pioneer 10
pioneer10.blurb: First craft through the asteroid belt and past Jupiter. Contact lost 2003; still coasting toward Aldebaran.

pioneer11.name: Pioneer 11
pioneer11.blurb: First Saturn flyby. Silent since 1995, drifting toward the constellation Aquila.

newhorizons.name: New Horizons
newhorizons.blurb: Pluto flyby 2015, Arrokoth 2019. Now exploring the Kuiper Belt from >60 AU out.

parker.name: Parker Solar Probe
parker.blurb: Fastest object ever built; repeatedly dives through the Sun's corona inside 0.05 AU.

solarorbiter.name: Solar Orbiter
solarorbiter.blurb: Imaging the Sun's poles from increasingly inclined orbits inside Mercury's orbit.

bepicolombo.name: BepiColombo
bepicolombo.blurb: Dual orbiters en route to Mercury via nine planetary flybys; orbital insertion late 2026.

juice.name: JUICE
juice.blurb: Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer — will orbit Ganymede in the 2030s after Earth/Venus gravity assists.

lucy.name: Lucy
lucy.blurb: Touring a record number of Jupiter Trojan asteroids across two swarms through 2033.

psyche.name: Psyche
psyche.blurb: Heading to metal asteroid 16 Psyche, arriving 2029 — a possible exposed planetary core.

europaclipper.name: Europa Clipper
europaclipper.blurb: Largest planetary craft NASA has built; Mars gravity assist 2025, Jupiter orbit 2030, then ~50 Europa flybys.

osirisapex.name: OSIRIS-APEX
osirisapex.blurb: Delivered Bennu samples in 2023; now chasing asteroid Apophis for its 2029 Earth flyby.

cassini.name: Cassini
cassini.blurb: 13 years orbiting Saturn; ended with a deliberate atmospheric plunge in 2017. Trajectory shown for its full mission.

juno.name: Juno
juno.blurb: Polar orbiter mapping Jupiter's interior and magnetosphere on elongated 53-day orbits.

kepler.name: Kepler
kepler.blurb: Planet-hunter that found 2,600+ exoplanets; retired 2018 into an Earth-trailing heliocentric orbit.

jwst.name: Webb (JWST)
jwst.blurb: Infrared observatory in a halo orbit around Sun-Earth L2, ~1.5M km from Earth.

gaia.name: Gaia
gaia.blurb: Mapped 1.8 billion stars from L2; science ops ended Jan 2025, now in a heliocentric retirement orbit.

soho.name: SOHO
soho.blurb: Solar watchdog at L1 since 1996; discovered 5,000+ comets grazing the Sun.

stereo_a.name: STEREO-A
stereo_a.blurb: Solar observatory drifting ahead of Earth's orbit, giving stereoscopic views of coronal mass ejections.

hera.name: Hera
hera.blurb: Planetary-defense mission cruising to Dimorphos to survey DART's impact crater (arrival 2026).

hayabusa2.name: Hayabusa2
hayabusa2.blurb: Returned Ryugu samples in 2020; extended mission targets asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031.

maven.name: MAVEN
maven.blurb: Mars orbiter studying atmospheric loss; heliocentric track follows Mars' orbit.

dart.name: DART
dart.blurb: First planetary-defense test — deliberately slammed into Dimorphos and changed its orbit. Full mission path shown.
